headline: Goldman backs off, but local models keep getting bigger
summary: Goldman pulls Claude Code; an open-source project squeezes a 284B model into 64G of RAM.

items.title: Goldman takes Claude Code off the shelf
items.pitch: Goldman pulled Claude Code away from its bankers, and HN blew up over it. Companies rolling out AI isn't always a straight line up, so it's worth keeping an eye on how things go at your own company.
why: 793 points and 422 comments on HN, the enterprise crowd really is talking about it
Banks are the most conservative customers, so a retreat like this spreads fast
If your company is evaluating AI coding tools right now, this is a real live example
actions: Read the original report and the HN thread, and think through where you draw the line on AI tools you buy
Talk to your IT/compliance folks: is it deployed, and can audits keep up
deep_dive: Don't just read the headline: this is about a company pulling back a coding tool it had already deployed, not about the model getting worse.
It's relevant if you work at a multinational company, since AI rollouts often fail on compliance, audits, and actual payoff, not on capability.
items.signals: 793 points on HN · 422 comments · hit the top five within 17 hours

items.title: 284B DeepSeek squeezed into 64G of RAM
items.pitch: Someone open-sourced a project that gets the 284B DeepSeek running on a 64G machine with no GPU. Your Mac mini might be able to run a big model locally too.
why: No GPU needed, which saves on GPU costs and dodges privacy worries
432 points and 193 comments on HN, the community is testing it out
Local means your data never leaves the machine, good for sensitive spreadsheets
actions: Try a small model on your Mac first, then decide if you want to wrestle with the 284B
deep_dive: Unlike the cloud Claude/Codex you use now, this puts the weights on your own machine, so it runs even offline.
The tradeoff is it'll probably be really slow (a few characters per second), and 284B is a tight fit for 64G of RAM, so it's mostly leaning on SSD swap.
Non-developers can try it, but don't expect it to feel as smooth as Opus 5.5.
items.signals: 432 points on HN · 193 comments · GitHub repo already open source

items.title: Collapse the PR descriptions AI writes
items.pitch: Simon Willison's tip: tuck the wordy AI-generated PR notes into a collapsible block, and the review page instantly gets cleaner.
why: Read the summary first, expand the details if you want more
Just wrap the long description in HTML <details>
It's what he does when he opens PRs with Claude Code / Codex
